# We find the work. We help you win it.

Find the council and public contracts worth bidding for, and put in a stronger bid.

No commission. You keep 100% of what you win.

Tendderr is an independent service for small and mid-sized contractors in England, Wales and Northern Ireland. We find suitable public-sector opportunities for your kind of work, help you decide which ones are worth your time, and can prepare the tender submission for you.

## A practical service for busy contractors

Tendderr helps established contractors find and compete for public-sector work without spending hours searching procurement websites and completing paperwork.

We take a straightforward approach: find suitable opportunities, check whether they're worth pursuing and agree a fixed fee before undertaking any bid preparation.

## What we offer

Three things are free and carry no obligation. Everything else is paid, at a fixed fee agreed with you before any work starts, and we never take a commission on contracts you win.

Free

### A personalised tender alert

Tell us what work you do and where. A person matches public-sector opportunities to your business, and our contract renewal alerts flag contracts nearing expiry, so you can get ready before they’re re-tendered.

We’ll review a tender’s main requirements, deadlines and potential barriers to help you decide whether it deserves a closer look. Writing it yourself? We’ll review one bid answer free.

Fixed fee

### Professional bid preparation

No commission. You keep 100% of what you win; you pay a fixed fee for the work, agreed before it starts.

## Get ready before the work comes back round

Included free in your tender alert

### Contract renewal alerts

Many public contracts run for a fixed term and then go back out to tender. We track public contracts nearing expiry, using published contract and award notices, and flag the ones that fit your business, so you can prepare before the re-tender: get registered, line up policies and accreditations, and get onto the right framework or dynamic market in time.

## Frameworks, DPSs and dynamic markets, explained

A lot of repeat council, school and housing work isn’t advertised as a one-off tender. It’s bought through one of these three. Here’s the difference, in plain English.

Framework

### A list of approved suppliers, set up for several years

A buyer, or a buying organisation acting for many buyers, picks a group of suppliers for a set period. Individual contracts (“call-offs”) are then awarded to suppliers on the list, directly or through a mini-competition.

When you can join: usually only when it’s tendered. Miss the window and you may wait years for the next one.

Dynamic purchasing system (DPS)

### Like a framework, but open to new suppliers

Set up under the old rules (the Public Contracts Regulations 2015). Buyers invite suppliers on the DPS to bid for each contract. New ones are now set up as dynamic markets instead, but existing DPSs carry on until they end.

When you can join: at any time during the DPS’s life.

Dynamic market

### The new version, under the Procurement Act 2023

Buyers get a list of pre-approved suppliers who have passed set checks (the “conditions of participation”). Contracts are then competed between suppliers on the market.

When you can join: at any time, and approved suppliers must be added within a reasonable time.

A place on any of these is permission to compete for work through it, not a promise of work. It can still be one of the best routes into steady public-sector contracts. Source: Government Commercial Agency (https://www.gca.gov.uk/how-to-supply/dynamic-market).

1April 2026

New rule

### Won a public contract? You may now need to be registered.

Since 1 April 2026, a supplier awarded a notifiable contract (worth £30,000 or more including VAT for councils and most other public bodies, or £12,000 or more for central government, including NHS bodies) must register on the government’s Central Digital Platform and give the buyer its unique identifier. Registration is free.

Our bid-ready pack includes doing this with you on a call, signed in under your own GOV.UK One Login.

Sources: New legislative requirements under the Procurement Act 2023, GOV.UK (https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/procurement-act-2023-short-guides/new-legislative-requirements-under-the-procurement-act-2023-html); How to register and find your unique identifier, GOV.UK (https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/procurement-act-2023-short-guides/how-to-register-your-organisation-and-find-your-unique-identifier-a-guide-for-suppliers-html). Wales already had a similar rule under its own regulations.

Public-sector work can be steady and well run, but finding it and bidding for it takes time most small firms don't have.

### The right contracts

Spend your time on opportunities that suit your size, your skills and your patch, not on ones you were never likely to win.

### No missed deadlines

Hear about suitable opportunities in good time, so you're not finding out about them after the closing date.

How local government procurement spend in England was split, 2024

- 23% directly with local SMEs (£18.4bn)

- 12% with SMEs based elsewhere (£9.7bn)

- 65% with all other suppliers

Source: British Chambers of Commerce & Tussell, SME Procurement Tracker 2025 (PDF) (https://www.britishchambers.org.uk/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/BCC-Tussell-AutogenAI-SME-PROCUREMENT-TRACKER-2025.pdf) (2024 figures)

## Common questions

### Do I need experience of public contracts?

No. Many of the firms we speak to have never bid for public work. We’ll explain what’s involved in plain terms and help you judge whether an opportunity is realistic for your business.

### What does the free suitability check involve?

You send us a specific opportunity. We review what the buyer wants, what they’re asking bidders to provide and how it fits your business, and point out the main requirements, deadlines and potential barriers, to help you decide whether the opportunity deserves a closer look. It’s an initial check, not a full assessment or a bid, and there’s no obligation.

### How are fees set?

Every paid service has a fixed fee, agreed with you before any work starts. Our prices are published as “from” prices: framework applications from £795, DPS or dynamic market applications from £395, and bid packs from £495 (Essential), £750 (Standard) or £995 (Complete). See services and prices. Prices have no VAT added: Tendderr isn’t VAT registered. The tender alert, the initial suitability check and a review of one bid answer are free.

### How quickly will I get a quote?

We’ll send a fixed quote within 2 working days of receiving your tender documents. Email the documents, or a link to the tender, to hello@tendderr.com.

### Do you take a commission if we win?

No commission. You keep 100% of what you win; you pay a fixed fee for the work, agreed before any work starts. There are no success fees or win fees.

### Do you use AI?

Yes. Our bids are AI-assisted, then reviewed and prepared by a person before anything goes to you. Calls to 0333 339 7931 are answered by a real person. Our online chat assistant is automated.

### What’s the Central Digital Platform, and do I need to register?

It’s the government’s online service (part of Find a Tender) where suppliers register and get a unique identifier. Since 1 April 2026, if you win a notifiable public contract (£30,000 or more including VAT for councils and most public bodies, or £12,000 or more for central government, including NHS bodies), you must register and give the buyer your identifier. Registration is free. See our step-by-step registration guide, or we can do it with you on a call as part of our bid-ready pack.

### Do I have to pay to see public-sector tenders?

No. The government’s own guidance says Find a Tender, the central platform for UK public procurement notices, is free and you shouldn’t have to pay to view opportunities. Our tender alert is free too: we add a person checking each match, other portals such as Sell2Wales and eTendersNI, and contract renewal alerts for contracts nearing expiry. See where to find public-sector tenders.

### What changed under the Procurement Act 2023?

New rules for most public-sector buying in England, Wales and Northern Ireland started on 24 February 2025. Notices and supplier registration moved to one free central platform, there’s a new competitive flexible procedure, frameworks can be more open, and buyers must give an assessment summary for every assessed final tender. Read our plain-English guide to the Procurement Act 2023.

### We lost a tender. Can you help us challenge it?

We can help you understand why you lost marks and plan a stronger bid next time, through our lost-bid review. We don’t give legal advice or advise on whether to challenge a decision. For that, speak to a solicitor, or raise a concern with the government’s Public Procurement Review Service (https://www.gov.uk/guidance/procurement-compliance-oversight).

### Can you guarantee we’ll win?

No one honestly can. Buyers make the decision. What we can do is help you pick opportunities that suit you and put forward a clear, complete bid.

### Do you cover Scotland or Ireland?

We cover England, Wales and Northern Ireland. Northern Ireland firms can also get alerts for, and help bidding on, Republic of Ireland public tenders on eTenders. These follow different rules (for example, tax clearance), and we’ll explain what’s involved. We don’t currently cover Scotland.

### How do I get started?

Email hello@tendderr.com with a line or two about what your business does and where you work, or call 0333 339 7931. We’ll get back to you.

# Framework, DPS and dynamic-market applications

## Frameworks, DPSs and dynamic markets, explained

Much repeat public-sector work is bought through one of these, rather than advertised as a one-off tender.

Framework

### A list of approved suppliers, set up for several years

A buyer, or a buying organisation acting for many buyers, picks a group of suppliers for a set period. Individual contracts (“call-offs”) are then awarded to suppliers on the list, directly or through a mini-competition.

When you can join: usually only when it’s tendered. Miss the window and you may wait years for the next one.

Dynamic purchasing system (DPS)

### Like a framework, but open to new suppliers

Set up under the old rules (the Public Contracts Regulations 2015). Buyers invite suppliers on the DPS to bid for each contract. New ones are now set up as dynamic markets instead, but existing DPSs carry on until they end.

When you can join: at any time during the DPS’s life.

Dynamic market

### The new version, under the Procurement Act 2023

Buyers get a list of pre-approved suppliers who have passed set checks (the “conditions of participation”). Contracts are then competed between suppliers on the market.

When you can join: at any time, and approved suppliers must be added within a reasonable time.

A place on any of these is permission to compete for work through it, not a promise of work. It can still be one of the best routes into steady public-sector contracts. Source: Government Commercial Agency (https://www.gca.gov.uk/how-to-supply/dynamic-market).

## What we do

We look for the frameworks, DPSs and dynamic markets that suit your trade and area, and tell you in your free alert when ones that fit you open or reopen. When you want to apply, we check the entry requirements with you and prepare the application.

## Be realistic about what a place gives you

Getting onto a framework, DPS or dynamic market lets you compete for the contracts awarded through it. It doesn’t guarantee work. Buyers still choose between suppliers, often through a mini-competition, so we’ll be honest about which ones are worth your time.

## Prices

DPS or dynamic market applicationFrom £395
Full framework applicationFrom £795

Fixed fee, no commission, no win fee. Prices have no VAT added: Tendderr isn’t VAT registered. The exact fee is agreed before we start.

## What’s included

- Finding the frameworks, DPSs and dynamic markets that fit you
- Opening and reopening dates in your free alert
- Checking the entry requirements (conditions of participation) with you
- Preparing the application answers with you, ready for you to submit
- Getting your Central Digital Platform details ready to share

## Worked example
A commercial cleaning firm wants to join a council’s cleaning dynamic market. We check the conditions of participation with it, list the documents it needs, such as insurance certificates and policies, and prepare the application answers for it to check and submit. Fee: from £395, agreed before we start. A full framework application, with a larger quality section, starts from £795.
Illustrative example, not a real client.

## Questions about framework applications

### Do I have to pay the buyer to join a framework?

Not for access. Under the Procurement Act 2023, buyers can’t charge suppliers to be on a framework or dynamic market. Fees can only be charged as a fixed percentage of contracts you’re awarded. Our own fee is fixed: from £395 for a DPS or dynamic market and from £795 for a full framework, with no commission.

### When can I apply?

Dynamic markets must accept applications at any time. Frameworks are usually only open when tendered, though open frameworks must reopen at least once in their first three years. Our free alert tells you when the ones that fit you open or reopen.

### Does a framework place guarantee work?

No. It’s permission to compete for, or be awarded, work through it. It isn’t a promise of work.

Our services

# Bid-ready pack

What a first-time bidder needs in place before their first tender: platform registration, core policies and a capability statement.

£195

Fixed fee, no commission, no win fee. Prices have no VAT added: Tendderr isn’t VAT registered.

1April 2026

New rule

### Won a public contract? You may now need to be registered.

Since 1 April 2026, a supplier awarded a notifiable contract (worth £30,000 or more including VAT for councils and most other public bodies, or £12,000 or more for central government, including NHS bodies) must register on the government’s Central Digital Platform and give the buyer its unique identifier. Registration is free.

Our bid-ready pack includes doing this with you on a call, signed in under your own GOV.UK One Login.

Sources: New legislative requirements under the Procurement Act 2023, GOV.UK (https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/procurement-act-2023-short-guides/new-legislative-requirements-under-the-procurement-act-2023-html); How to register and find your unique identifier, GOV.UK (https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/procurement-act-2023-short-guides/how-to-register-your-organisation-and-find-your-unique-identifier-a-guide-for-suppliers-html). Wales already had a similar rule under its own regulations.

## What’s in the pack

### 1. Central Digital Platform registration

We do this with you on a call. You sign in with your own GOV.UK One Login and we guide you through each step; we never log in for you. At the end you’ll have your unique identifier ready to give to buyers.

### 2. Six core policies

Buyers often ask to see standard policies. We draft six core policies based on how your firm actually works, for you to check, adopt and sign as your own.

### 3. A one-page capability statement

A clear summary of what your firm does, where and for whom, that you can attach to bids and send to buyers.

## Credited against a later bid pack

If you then ask us to prepare a bid pack, the £195 is credited against it.

- The £195 credited against a later bid pack

We then draft six core policies for the firm to adopt, and a one-page capability statement. Fee: £195. If the firm later orders a bid pack, the £195 comes off that fee.

## Questions about the bid-ready pack

Yes. The platform is free for everyone. Our £195 covers doing it with you on a call, plus six core policies and a one-page capability statement. The fee is credited against a later bid pack.

No. You sign in to your own GOV.UK One Login and account yourself. We guide you through it on the call.

### I don’t have a Companies House number. Can I still register?

Yes. If you don’t have a registry number, the platform generates a unique identifier for you.

## What we do

Send us the buyer’s feedback (for contracts run under the Procurement Act 2023, this is usually an assessment summary explaining how your bid was scored) and a copy of your bid. We’ll give you:

- A plain-English breakdown of where you scored well and where you lost marks
- The gaps that cost you, and how to close them
- Who won the contract, where that’s been published
- When the work is likely to come back out to tender

## What we don’t do

This isn’t legal advice. We don’t advise on legal challenges or on whether to challenge a decision. If you think a procurement was run unfairly, speak to a solicitor, or raise a concern with the government’s Public Procurement Review Service (https://www.gov.uk/guidance/procurement-compliance-oversight).

Illustrative example, not a real client.

## Questions about the lost-bid review

### What is an assessment summary?

Under the Procurement Act 2023, the buyer must give each supplier that submitted an assessed tender a written assessment summary before publishing the contract award notice. It explains how your tender was scored.

### How long do I have to raise concerns?

Where a standstill period applies, it’s at least eight working days from the day the contract award notice is published. We don’t give legal advice. For a formal challenge, speak to a solicitor.

### Is it free for bid clients?

Yes. The lost-bid review is free if we prepared the bid with you. Otherwise it’s £125.

## What we do

You also get a commitments register you can reuse and update for later bids.

Social value commitments usually become part of the contract, and buyers ask you to report on them. We keep them realistic for a firm your size, rather than inflating them to chase marks.

Standalone, for a bid you’re writing yourself£245

Illustrative example, not a real client.

## Questions about social value plans

### How much is social value worth in a tender?

For central government above-threshold procurements under PPN 002, at least 10% of the total score. From 1 January 2027, PPN 026 sets minimums of 10% or 20% for central government procurements of £1m or more.

### Will we be held to our commitments?

Yes. Commitments go into the contract as terms or KPIs. That’s why we only write commitments you can actually deliver.

### How much is the plan?

£145 as an add-on to a bid pack, or £245 standalone.

Title: Cleaning Tenders and Public Sector Cleaning Contracts | Tendderr
Summary: Cleaning tenders from councils, schools, NHS trusts and housing associations in England, Wales and NI. Free tender alerts, fixed-fee bid help, no win fee.

Public-sector tenders for

# Commercial cleaning

Office, school, campus, clinic and communal-area cleaning, window cleaning and periodic deep cleans.

Free tender alerts and suitability checks. Fixed fee, no commission, no win fee.

Find contracts for my business

Stock photo, for illustration.

## Who buys it

- Councils (offices, libraries, leisure and community buildings)
- Schools and academy trusts
- NHS trusts
- Universities and colleges
- Housing associations (communal areas and empty homes)

## The kind of work we look for

- Daily and contract cleaning of offices and public buildings
- School and academy trust cleaning, often bought through trust-wide frameworks
- Window and facade cleaning
- Washroom, deep and periodic cleans

Much of this work is bought through frameworks, DPSs and dynamic markets as well as one-off tenders. We look for both.

## Commercial cleaning tenders: common questions

### Where are commercial cleaning tenders advertised?

Public bodies such as councils, schools and academy trusts, nhs trusts, universities and colleges publish notices on Find a Tender, the government’s free central digital platform. Many also use regional portals, such as Sell2Wales in Wales, eTendersNI in Northern Ireland and YORtender for many Yorkshire councils. A lot of repeat work is bought through frameworks and dynamic markets. Our free tender alert covers all of these. See where to find public-sector tenders.

### Can a small commercial cleaning business win public-sector contracts?

Yes, the rules are designed to help. For regulated below-threshold contracts, buyers can’t use a separate pre-qualification stage to shortlist suppliers, because GOV.UK guidance recognises it can be a barrier for SMEs. Buyers may also reserve some below-threshold competitions for SMEs or local suppliers. If you’re not ready to bid direct, subcontracting to a main contractor is another route in.

### Is social value scored in these tenders?

Often. Central government buyers must give social value at least a 10% weighting in above-threshold procurements under PPN 002. Councils and other buyers may choose to apply the same approach. See our social value guide.

### Do I need to register before I bid?

You register free on the Central Digital Platform (Find a Tender) when you’re ready to bid. From 1 April 2026, buyers awarding notifiable below-threshold contracts must get your unique identifier. See our registration guide.

### How much does Tendderr charge?

Tender alerts, the suitability check and a review of one bid answer are free. Bid packs are from £495 (Essential), £750 (Standard) or £995 (Complete); framework applications from £795; DPS or dynamic market applications from £395; the bid-ready pack is £195. No commission: you keep 100% of what you win.

Answer eleven quick questions to see what you already have in place and what to sort before you bid for public-sector work.

Free. This tool runs entirely in your browser. Nothing you enter is sent to us or stored, and there’s no sign-up.

Show my next stepsStart again

## Your next steps

- Register free on Find a Tender. See our registration guide, or we can do it with you on a call in the bid-ready pack.
- Complete your core supplier information on the Central Digital Platform and keep it up to date. Buyers ask you to share it.
- Register on the portals for your area and pick the categories that match your trade. See where to find tenders, or ask for our free tender alert.
- Write policies that reflect how your firm actually works. Our bid-ready pack includes six core policies for you to adopt.
- Check what the tender documents ask for: buyers often set minimum cover levels. Gather your current certificates.
- Have your latest accounts ready. Buyers may check your financial standing as part of the conditions of participation.
- Write short summaries of recent, similar jobs: what you did, for whom, its size and how it went. Ask your contacts first.
- Check which accreditations the tender asks for. If you don’t hold them yet, consider a smaller lot or our subcontracting route in the meantime.
- Be honest about capacity. A smaller lot, a partner, or subcontracting to a main contractor may suit you better for now.
- Use our social value checklist, or ask about a social value plan.
- Work back from the deadline with our tender timeline calculator. If time is tight, say so early.

This checklist doesn’t predict whether you’d win: buyers decide that, on the tender in front of them. It shows what to sort before you bid.

Want a second opinion on a specific tender? Our suitability check is free, and we’ll review one bid answer free too: email hello@tendderr.com.

## About this tool

The questions cover what buyers commonly ask for: registration, policies, insurance, finances, experience, capacity, social value and time. Every tender sets its own requirements, so always check the tender documents too.
This tool runs entirely in your browser. Nothing you enter is sent to us or stored, and there’s no sign-up.

- How to register your organisation and find your unique identifier: a guide for suppliers (GOV.UK) (https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/procurement-act-2023-short-guides/how-to-register-your-organisation-and-find-your-unique-identifier-a-guide-for-suppliers-html)

## Questions about this tool

### Does this tell me whether I’ll win?

No. Buyers decide who wins, based on the tender in front of them. This checklist only shows what to sort before you bid.

### Is anything I enter saved or sent to you?

No. This tool runs entirely in your browser. Nothing you enter is sent to us or stored, and there’s no sign-up.

### What if I’m not ready yet?

That’s common. Start with the basics: platform registration, policies and certificates. Our bid-ready pack (£195) covers registration, six core policies and a capability statement, and the fee comes off a later bid pack.

URL: https://tendderr.com/tools/social-value-checklist.html
Title: Social Value and PPN 002 Checklist for Tenders | Tendderr
Summary: Free social value checklist for tenders, based on GOV.UK guidance: PPN 002 now and the PPN 026 Social Value Model from 1 January 2027.

Free tool

# Social value and PPN checklist

Check your social value answer against GOV.UK guidance before you submit, including PPN 002 now and PPN 026 from 1 January 2027.

Free. This tool runs entirely in your browser. Nothing you enter is sent to us or stored, and there’s no sign-up.

0 of 14 ticked

Understand what the buyer is scoring

- Find the social value question(s) in the tender documents, and the weighting given to them.
- Check which outcomes or themes the buyer says it wants, and answer those rather than a generic list.
- Check who the buyer is. PPN 002 applies to central government above-threshold procurements, with a minimum 10% social value weighting. Other public bodies, such as councils, may choose to apply it. Source: PPN 002, GOV.UK (https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/ppn-002-taking-account-of-social-value-in-the-award-of-contracts/ppn-002-taking-account-of-social-value-in-the-award-of-central-government-contracts-html).
- Note the word limit and any template or format the buyer asks you to use.

Make commitments you can deliver

- Give each commitment a number, an owner and a date, rather than a general intention.
- Make the commitments specific to this contract and the area it covers.
- Size them for a firm your size, so you can actually deliver them.
- If you’ll create jobs to deliver a central government contract, plan to advertise them through the government’s ‘Find a Job’ website, as PPN 002 requires. Source: PPN 002, GOV.UK (https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/ppn-002-taking-account-of-social-value-in-the-award-of-contracts/ppn-002-taking-account-of-social-value-in-the-award-of-central-government-contracts-html).

Show how you’ll report

- Expect your commitments to become part of the contract, as contract terms or KPIs, and to report on them. Source: PPN 002, GOV.UK (https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/ppn-002-taking-account-of-social-value-in-the-award-of-contracts/ppn-002-taking-account-of-social-value-in-the-award-of-central-government-contracts-html).
- Say how and how often you’ll measure and report progress.
- Keep a commitments register you can update and reuse for later bids.

Ready for PPN 026 (from 1 January 2027)

- For central government covered procurements of £1 million or more, PPN 026 sets a minimum social value weighting of 10% (£1 million to under £5 million) or 20% (£5 million or more). Source: PPN 026, GOV.UK (https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/ppn-026-the-social-value-model/ppn-026-the-social-value-model-html).
- It focuses on Good Jobs and Skills outcomes. Think now about the jobs, training and skills you could realistically offer.
- Contracts of £5 million or more need at least one social value KPI, and poor performance can be considered for exclusion, so only promise what you can deliver.

Print this checklistUntick all

## About this tool

Social value is how your firm will benefit the area the contract serves: for example local jobs, apprenticeships, work with schools or charities, or cutting emissions. The Public Services (Social Value) Act 2012 requires public bodies to consider social value when buying services. Read more in our social value guide.
This tool runs entirely in your browser. Nothing you enter is sent to us or stored, and there’s no sign-up.

### Sources

- PPN 002: taking account of social value in the award of central government contracts (GOV.UK, updated 5 March 2025) (https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/ppn-002-taking-account-of-social-value-in-the-award-of-contracts/ppn-002-taking-account-of-social-value-in-the-award-of-central-government-contracts-html)
- PPN 026: the Social Value Model (GOV.UK, updated 28 October 2026) (https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/ppn-026-the-social-value-model/ppn-026-the-social-value-model-html)

## Questions about this tool

### Does PPN 002 apply to council tenders?

PPN 002 applies to central government above-threshold procurements. Councils and other public bodies may choose to apply the same approach, so check the tender documents.

### What changes on 1 January 2027?

PPN 026 sets minimum social value weightings for central government covered procurements of £1 million or more: 10% from £1 million to under £5 million, and 20% for £5 million or more, focused on Good Jobs and Skills outcomes.

### Can you write it for us?

Yes. A social value plan is £145 as an add-on to a bid pack, or £245 standalone, and it’s included in the Complete bid pack.

Summary: Public-sector tenders in England: Find a Tender, Contracts Finder and regional portals such as YORtender, plus Central Digital Platform registration. Free alerts.

Public-sector tenders in

# England

Find, and bid for, council, school, NHS and housing association contracts across England.

Free tender alerts. Fixed fee, no commission, no win fee.

## Where tenders are published

Find a Tender is the central digital platform under the Procurement Act 2023. It’s free for everyone, with free search and alerts. Find a Tender (https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/)

Contracts Finder holds older notices and contracts. Contracts Finder (https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/)

Many buyers also use regional portals. In Yorkshire and the Humber, many public bodies use YORtender, including Wakefield Council and the West Yorkshire Combined Authority. Sources: Wakefield Council (https://www.wakefield.gov.uk/business/procurement-and-tendering/selling-to-the-council); West Yorkshire Combined Authority (https://www.westyorks-ca.gov.uk/governance/procurement/).

## Rules worth knowing

Since 24 February 2025, most public-sector buying in England has followed the Procurement Act 2023. Source: GOV.UK short guide for suppliers (https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/procurement-act-2023-short-guides/the-procurement-act-2023-a-short-guide-for-suppliers-html).

Since 1 April 2026, a supplier awarded a notifiable contract (worth £30,000 or more including VAT for councils and most other public bodies, or £12,000 or more for central government, including NHS bodies) must register on the Central Digital Platform and give the buyer its unique identifier. Registration is free. Source: New legislative requirements, GOV.UK (https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/procurement-act-2023-short-guides/new-legislative-requirements-under-the-procurement-act-2023-html).

- Free alerts from Find a Tender and regional portals, matched by a person
- Contract renewal alerts for contracts nearing expiry
- Framework, DPS and dynamic market applications
- Fixed-fee bid packs, from £495

## Tenders in England: common questions

### Do I have to pay to see tenders in England?

No. Find a Tender is free for everyone, with free search and alerts. Our tender alert is free too.

### Where do Yorkshire councils advertise?

Many Yorkshire and Humber public bodies use YORtender, as well as Find a Tender. See where to find tenders.

### Do I need to register before I bid?

You can register free on the Central Digital Platform when you’re ready to bid. Since 1 April 2026, you must be registered, and give the buyer your unique identifier, if you’re awarded a notifiable contract.

Title: Public Sector Tenders in Wales: Sell2Wales Help | Tendderr
Summary: Public-sector tenders in Wales: Sell2Wales, the Welsh Digital Platform, Central Digital Platform registration and the Welsh rules. Free alerts, fixed-fee bid help.

Public-sector tenders in

# Wales

Find, and bid for, Welsh council, school, NHS and housing association contracts on Sell2Wales and Find a Tender.

Free tender alerts. Fixed fee, no commission, no win fee.

## Where tenders are published

Sell2Wales is the Welsh Digital Platform, set up under the Procurement (Wales) Regulations 2024. Devolved Welsh contracting authorities must publish their notices through it, and it forwards them to the Central Digital Platform, so they also appear on Find a Tender. Source: Welsh Digital Platform guidance, GOV.WALES (https://www.gov.wales/procurement-act-2023-welsh-digital-platform-html).

Sell2Wales also lists subcontracting opportunities. Sell2Wales (https://www.sell2wales.gov.wales/)

## Rules worth knowing

Devolved Welsh contracting authorities are regulated by the Procurement Act 2023, with some differences. The Welsh Government has made its own regulations (for example, notices can contain different information), and the Wales procurement policy statement applies instead of the national procurement policy statement. Source: devolved contracting authorities guidance, GOV.UK (https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/procurement-act-2023-guidance-documents-plan-phase/guidance-devolved-contracting-authorities-html).

Register on the Central Digital Platform first. Suppliers need to register on the Central Digital Platform to get a unique identifier, and complete their core supplier information. Sell2Wales asks you to enter that unique identifier in your Sell2Wales company profile so you can keep tendering. Sources: GOV.WALES (https://www.gov.wales/procurement-act-2023-welsh-digital-platform-html); Sell2Wales (https://www.sell2wales.gov.wales/helpandresources/cdp/procurementact2023/).

Sell2Wales also reminds suppliers about the 30-day payment term that applies in public sub-contracts. Source: Sell2Wales (https://www.sell2wales.gov.wales/helpandresources/cdp/procurementact2023/).

- Free alerts from Sell2Wales and Find a Tender, matched by a person

On Sell2Wales, the Welsh Digital Platform. Devolved Welsh authorities must publish their notices through it, and Sell2Wales forwards them to the Central Digital Platform, so they also appear on Find a Tender.

### Do I need to register on the Central Digital Platform to bid in Wales?

Yes. Register on the Central Digital Platform to get your unique identifier, complete your core supplier information, then add the identifier to your Sell2Wales company profile.

### Are the rules different in Wales?

Devolved Welsh authorities follow the Procurement Act 2023 with some differences: the Welsh Government made its own regulations, and the Wales procurement policy statement applies instead of the national one.

Public-sector tenders in

# Northern Ireland

Find, and bid for, Northern Ireland public contracts on eTendersNI and Find a Tender, with cross-border support on Irish eTenders.

Free tender alerts. Fixed fee, no commission, no win fee.

## Where tenders are published

eTendersNI is free. Register, choose the CPV categories that match your work, and the Administrator on your account receives email alerts. The Department of Finance lists a helpdesk on 0800 240 4545. Source: Department of Finance NI (https://www.finance-ni.gov.uk/articles/register-email-alerts-ni-public-sector-tender-opportunities). Registering needs a D-U-N-S number, which is free to get. Source: eTendersNI questions and answers, Department of Finance NI (https://www.finance-ni.gov.uk/articles/common-questions-and-answers-about-etendersni).

Competitions on eTendersNI that need a Procurement Act 2023 notice are also published on Find a Tender. Others appear only on eTendersNI. Find a Tender is free. Source: eTendersNI notice, 2 February 2026 (https://etendersni.gov.uk/epps/viewInfo.do?entryId=6381479&sec=newItems).

Northern Ireland firms can also bid for Republic of Ireland public tenders on Irish eTenders. These follow different rules, for example tax clearance. Sources: eTenders (https://www.etenders.gov.ie/); Revenue (https://www.revenue.ie/en/starting-a-business/tax-clearance/when-is-a-tax-clearance-certificate-required/to-apply-for-certain-grants-and-public-sector-contracts.aspx).

## Rules worth knowing

Transferred Northern Ireland authorities are regulated by the Procurement Act 2023, with some differences. The national procurement policy statement doesn’t apply to them. Source: devolved contracting authorities guidance, GOV.UK (https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/procurement-act-2023-guidance-documents-plan-phase/guidance-devolved-contracting-authorities-html).

Share codes. To bid for above-threshold or notifiable competitions, register on Find a Tender and share your details with the buyer using a share code. Source: eTendersNI (https://etendersni.gov.uk/epps/viewInfo.do?entryId=6381479&sec=newItems). The Education Authority, for example, asks suppliers tendering on eTendersNI to provide their PPON (unique identifier) and share code, or the tender may be rejected. Source: Education Authority NI (https://www.eani.org.uk/procurement/supplier-tender-support).

## Tenders in Northern Ireland: common questions

### Is eTendersNI free?

Yes. eTendersNI is free to register, and you’ll need a D-U-N-S number, which is also free to get.

### Do NI tenders appear on Find a Tender?

Competitions on eTendersNI that need a Procurement Act 2023 notice are also published on Find a Tender. Others appear only on eTendersNI, so it’s worth registering on both.

### What is a share code?

It’s how you share your Central Digital Platform details with a buyer. For above-threshold or notifiable competitions on eTendersNI, you register on Find a Tender and give the buyer your share code. Some buyers say a tender without one may be rejected.

### Can you help with Republic of Ireland tenders?

Yes. Northern Ireland firms can get alerts for, and help bidding on, Irish eTenders. These follow different rules, for example tax clearance, and we’ll explain what’s involved.

Title: Procurement Act 2023 Explained for Small Suppliers | Tendderr
Summary: Procurement Act 2023 in plain English for small suppliers: 2026 thresholds, below-threshold rules, assessment summaries, standstill and payment. GOV.UK sourced.

Guide

# The Procurement Act 2023: what small contractors need to know

Last checked against official sources: 30 October 2026. General information, not legal advice.

Short answer
Since 24 February 2025, most public-sector buying in England, Wales and Northern Ireland has followed the Procurement Act 2023. For small suppliers the main changes are: one free central platform (Find a Tender) for notices and supplier registration, a new ‘competitive flexible’ procedure, more open frameworks, a written assessment summary for every assessed final tender, and 30-day payment terms on a broader range of public contracts.

## Who the Act covers

The government says the changes matter to anyone who supplies, or hopes to supply, goods, works or services to government departments, the NHS, local authorities, universities, schools, social housing organisations, police and fire services, and utility companies. Source: Cabinet Office short guide for suppliers (https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/procurement-act-2023-short-guides/the-procurement-act-2023-a-short-guide-for-suppliers-html).

Public procurement is devolved in Wales and Scotland and transferred in Northern Ireland. Welsh authorities follow the Act with some Welsh differences, and the Wales procurement policy statement applies instead of the national one. Devolved Scottish authorities keep using Scottish procurement law, which is why we don’t cover Scotland. Source: GOV.UK guidance on devolved contracting authorities (https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/procurement-act-2023-guidance-documents-plan-phase/guidance-devolved-contracting-authorities-html).

## What changed for suppliers

- One free platform. Find a Tender is the central digital platform for notices and supplier registration. It’s free for everyone, and you shouldn’t pay to view public-sector opportunities.

- A simpler, more flexible process. The Act brings in a new ‘competitive flexible’ procedure that lets buyers negotiate and work with bidders.

- More open frameworks. The aim is that suppliers aren’t shut out of frameworks for long periods. See our frameworks, DPS and dynamic markets guide.

- Feedback on every assessed final tender. Buyers must give bidders an assessment summary.

- Prompt payment. 30-day payment terms apply on a broader range of public contracts, including down the supply chain.

- Oversight. A new Procurement Review Unit includes the Public Procurement Review Service, where you can raise concerns about a specific procurement or late payment.

Source: Cabinet Office short guide for suppliers (https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/procurement-act-2023-short-guides/the-procurement-act-2023-a-short-guide-for-suppliers-html).

## The thresholds from 1 January 2026

Above these values a procurement is ‘covered’ by the full rules of the Act. Below them, the lighter below-threshold rules apply. Thresholds are revised every two years.

Procurement Act 2023 thresholds from 1 January 2026

| Type of contract | Threshold | 

| Goods and services: central government | £135,018 | 

| Goods and services: sub-central (for example councils) | £207,720 | 

| Works | £5,193,000 | 

| Light-touch services | £663,540 | 

| Utilities goods and services | £415,440 | 

| Defence and security goods and services | £415,440 | 

| Concessions | £5,193,000 | 

Source: PPN 023: 2026 threshold amounts (https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/ppn-023-2026-threshold-amounts/ppn-023-2026-threshold-amounts-html).

## Smaller contracts: the below-threshold rules

- No separate pre-qualification stage. For regulated below-threshold contracts, buyers can’t use a separate suitability stage (a PQQ) to shortlist. The guidance explains this is because it can be a barrier for SMEs and VCSEs. There’s an exception for higher-value below-threshold works.

- Notices go on Find a Tender first. Below-threshold tender notices must be published on the central digital platform.

- Reserved competitions. Buyers may reserve below-threshold competitions for SMEs and VCSEs, or for UK or local suppliers.

- Not every buyer. These rules don’t apply to schools or to transferred Northern Ireland authorities, unless a reserved or Welsh arrangement applies.

Source: GOV.UK guidance on below-threshold contracts (https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/procurement-act-2023-guidance-documents-define-phase/guidance-below-threshold-contracts-html).

From 1 April 2026, if you’re awarded a notifiable below-threshold contract (from £12,000 including VAT for central government and the NHS, or £30,000 for sub-central buyers such as councils), the buyer needs your unique supplier identifier from the central digital platform. Source: GOV.UK: new legislative requirements (https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/procurement-act-2023-short-guides/new-legislative-requirements-under-the-procurement-act-2023-html). Our registration guide explains how to get one.

## Assessment summaries and the standstill period

The buyer must give an assessment summary to each supplier that submitted an assessed tender, at the same time and before it publishes the contract award notice. It explains how your tender was assessed. Source: GOV.UK guidance on assessment summaries (https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/procurement-act-2023-guidance-documents-procure-phase/guidance-assessment-summaries-html).

Where a standstill period applies, it is at least eight working days, starting on the day the contract award notice is published. Source: GOV.UK guidance on contract award notices and standstill (https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/procurement-act-2023-guidance-documents-procure-phase/guidance-contract-award-notices-and-standstill-html).

Lost a bid? Our lost-bid review (£125) goes through your assessment summary with you and plans the next bid.

## Payment and contract transparency

- Since 1 January 2026, buyers must publish payments compliance notices showing how they’re meeting the 30-day payment terms. Each notice covers six months. Different timing applies to procurement regulated by the Welsh Ministers.

- For contracts procured under procedures that started on or after 1 April 2026, buyers must publish payments of more than £30,000 (including VAT) every quarter.

- On public contracts over £5 million where key performance indicators are set, buyers must publish a contract performance notice at least every 12 months.

Source: GOV.UK: new legislative requirements under the Procurement Act 2023 (https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/procurement-act-2023-short-guides/new-legislative-requirements-under-the-procurement-act-2023-html).

## Sources

- The Procurement Act 2023: a short guide for suppliers (Cabinet Office, GOV.UK) (https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/procurement-act-2023-short-guides/the-procurement-act-2023-a-short-guide-for-suppliers-html)
- Guidance: devolved contracting authorities (GOV.UK, updated 15 April 2026) (https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/procurement-act-2023-guidance-documents-plan-phase/guidance-devolved-contracting-authorities-html)
- PPN 023: 2026 threshold amounts (GOV.UK, published 27 November 2025) (https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/ppn-023-2026-threshold-amounts/ppn-023-2026-threshold-amounts-html)
- Guidance: below-threshold contracts (GOV.UK, updated 13 July 2026) (https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/procurement-act-2023-guidance-documents-define-phase/guidance-below-threshold-contracts-html)
- New legislative requirements under the Procurement Act 2023 (GOV.UK) (https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/procurement-act-2023-short-guides/new-legislative-requirements-under-the-procurement-act-2023-html)
- Guidance: assessment summaries (GOV.UK, updated 17 August 2026) (https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/procurement-act-2023-guidance-documents-procure-phase/guidance-assessment-summaries-html)
- Guidance: contract award notices and standstill (GOV.UK, updated 17 August 2026) (https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/procurement-act-2023-guidance-documents-procure-phase/guidance-contract-award-notices-and-standstill-html)

## Quick answers

### When did the Procurement Act 2023 come into force?

On 24 February 2025. Procurements that started before then carry on under the old rules.

### Does the Procurement Act 2023 apply in Scotland?

Devolved Scottish authorities continue to follow Scottish procurement law, so most Scottish public-sector buying isn’t run under the Act. Tendderr covers England, Wales and Northern Ireland, plus Irish eTenders.

### Do I have to pay to see public-sector tenders?

No. Find a Tender, the central digital platform, is free for everyone. The government says you should not pay to view public-sector opportunities.

### What are the procurement thresholds for 2026?

From 1 January 2026: £135,018 for central government goods and services, £207,720 for sub-central buyers such as councils, £5,193,000 for works and £663,540 for light-touch services (PPN 023).

### What is an assessment summary?

It’s the written feedback that the buyer must give every supplier that submitted an assessed tender, before the contract award notice is published. It explains how your tender was scored.

### How long is the standstill period?

At least eight working days, starting on the day the contract award notice is published.

Title: How to Register on the Central Digital Platform | Tendderr
Summary: Register free on the Central Digital Platform (Find a Tender) in three steps, get your unique identifier (PPON) and know what to have ready. GOV.UK sourced.

Guide

# How to register on the Central Digital Platform and get your unique identifier

Last checked against official sources: 30 October 2026. General information, not legal advice.

Short answer
Registration is free and done on Find a Tender in three steps: create a GOV.UK One Login, complete your Central Digital Platform account, then register your organisation as a supplier. You’ll get a unique identifier to share with buyers. You only need to register when you want to bid. Since 1 April 2026, if you win a notifiable below-threshold contract, the buyer must have your identifier.

## The three steps

- Create a GOV.UK One Login with your own work email address. You’ll get security codes by text message or an authenticator app. If you already have a One Login, sign in and skip to step 2.

- Complete your Central Digital Platform account. Agree to the privacy policy and enter your name.

- Register your organisation as a supplier. Enter your Companies House number or an equivalent such as a Charity Commission number. If you don’t have one, the platform gives you a unique identifier. Add your SME status, a shared organisation email address and your registered address. Then save and select ‘View’ to see your identifier.

One person sets up the account and becomes the Administrator. They can add and approve other users, and they enter and amend the organisation’s details. Source: GOV.UK guide to registering and finding your unique identifier (https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/procurement-act-2023-short-guides/how-to-register-your-organisation-and-find-your-unique-identifier-a-guide-for-suppliers-html).

## Basic registration for smaller contracts

For notifiable below-threshold contracts, you only need a basic registration to generate an identifier. GOV.UK describes it as a short five-minute registration. It asks for:

- organisation name
- organisation address (a non-UK address is allowed)
- email address
- Companies House or other registry number. If you don’t have one, a Public Procurement Organisation Number (PPON) is generated for you
- SME or VCSE status

From 1 April 2026, buyers must confirm you’re registered and get your identifier when they award a notifiable below-threshold contract. That’s £12,000 including VAT or more for central government and NHS bodies, and £30,000 or more for sub-central buyers. The same identifier is then used for all future procurements. Source: GOV.UK: new legislative requirements (https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/procurement-act-2023-short-guides/new-legislative-requirements-under-the-procurement-act-2023-html).

## What to have ready for bigger tenders

For tenders covered by the full rules, the government lists the information you’ll need. In summary:

- your Companies House number, if you have one
- postal address, website and email
- the last two years of accounts, if you have them
- details of any people or businesses connected to your business, or with significant control over it
- details of any convictions or offences by the organisation or connected people

Source: Cabinet Office short guide for suppliers (https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/procurement-act-2023-short-guides/the-procurement-act-2023-a-short-guide-for-suppliers-html).

## Registered on the old Find a Tender?

You need to re-register. If you use the same email address, your saved searches from the old account carry over. Source: Cabinet Office short guide for suppliers (https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/procurement-act-2023-short-guides/the-procurement-act-2023-a-short-guide-for-suppliers-html).

## Want a hand?

Our bid-ready pack (£195) does the registration with you on a call. You sign in to your own account yourself. It also includes six core policies and a one-page capability statement.

### How long does registration take?

GOV.UK describes the basic registration needed for below-threshold contracts as a short five-minute registration. Full supplier information for bigger tenders takes longer.

### What is a PPON?

Title: Frameworks, DPS and Dynamic Markets Explained | Tendderr
Summary: How frameworks, open frameworks, DPSs and dynamic markets work under the Procurement Act 2023: terms, reopening and fees. Sourced from GOV.UK.

Guide

# Frameworks, DPSs and dynamic markets: how to get on them

Last checked against official sources: 30 October 2026. General information, not legal advice.

Short answer
A framework is an agreement with selected suppliers that buyers then award contracts (‘call-offs’) through. Under the Procurement Act 2023 most frameworks last up to four years, and you usually can only join when one is tendered. Open frameworks reopen at least once in the first three years. A dynamic market, which replaces the dynamic purchasing system (DPS) under the Act, must accept new suppliers at any time. You can’t be charged just to be on a framework or dynamic market.

## Frameworks

- Term. Up to four years. For defence and security, and utilities frameworks, the limit is eight years. A longer term is allowed only if the nature of the work needs it, and the buyer must publish its reasons.

- Call-offs. Buyers award contracts under a framework either by a competitive selection process (a mini-competition) or without further competition, following the framework’s terms. Contract award notices must now be published for call-offs.

- Fees. Buyers can’t charge suppliers for access to a framework. Fees can only be charged to suppliers awarded a call-off contract, as a fixed percentage of its value.

Source: GOV.UK guidance on frameworks (https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/procurement-act-2023-guidance-documents-define-phase/guidance-frameworks-html).

## Open frameworks: a new chance to join

Open frameworks are new under the Act. They must be reopened to new suppliers at least once in the first three years, then at least every five years, up to a maximum total of eight years. When one reopens, new suppliers can join. A single-supplier open framework is limited to four years. Source: GOV.UK guidance on frameworks (https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/procurement-act-2023-guidance-documents-define-phase/guidance-frameworks-html).

## Dynamic markets (replacing the DPS)

- The Act replaces dynamic purchasing systems and qualification systems with a single tool called a dynamic market.

- Dynamic markets must stay open to new suppliers at any time. Buyers must consider applications within a reasonable time and admit suppliers who meet the conditions and aren’t excluded.

- Membership conditions must be proportionate. Buyers can’t ask for audited accounts from suppliers who aren’t required to have them audited under the Companies Act 2006. They also can’t require contract insurance to be in place before award, so you can commit to having it at award.

- For dynamic markets that aren’t utilities ones, fees can only be charged to suppliers awarded a contract, as a fixed percentage of its estimated value. They can’t be charged for membership.

Source: GOV.UK guidance on dynamic markets (https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/procurement-act-2023-guidance-documents-define-phase/guidance-dynamic-markets-html).

## Why you still see DPSs

The Act doesn’t apply to procurements started before 24 February 2025, or to contracts awarded through frameworks or dynamic purchasing systems set up under the previous rules. So older frameworks and DPSs are still in use alongside the new tools. Source: PPN 002, paragraph 6 (https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/ppn-002-taking-account-of-social-value-in-the-award-of-contracts/ppn-002-taking-account-of-social-value-in-the-award-of-central-government-contracts-html).

## Getting on the right ones

Many councils, schools and housing associations buy cleaning, grounds, maintenance and building work through frameworks and dynamic markets. Our free tender alert flags the ones that fit you when they open or reopen. Our framework and DPS applications service prepares the application with you: from £395 for a DPS or dynamic market, and from £795 for a full framework. No commission.

## Sources

- Guidance: frameworks (GOV.UK, updated 13 July 2026) (https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/procurement-act-2023-guidance-documents-define-phase/guidance-frameworks-html)
- Guidance: dynamic markets (GOV.UK, updated 13 July 2026) (https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/procurement-act-2023-guidance-documents-define-phase/guidance-dynamic-markets-html)
- PPN 002: taking account of social value in the award of central government contracts (GOV.UK, updated 5 March 2025) (https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/ppn-002-taking-account-of-social-value-in-the-award-of-contracts/ppn-002-taking-account-of-social-value-in-the-award-of-central-government-contracts-html)
- How to supply: dynamic markets (Government Commercial Agency) (https://www.gca.gov.uk/how-to-supply/dynamic-market)

## Quick answers

### Do I have to pay to join a public-sector framework?

Not for access. Under the Procurement Act 2023, buyers can’t charge suppliers to be on a framework. Fees can only be charged to suppliers awarded a call-off contract, as a fixed percentage of its value.

### How long does a framework last?

Usually up to four years (eight for defence and security, and utilities). Open frameworks must reopen at least once in the first three years and can last up to eight years in total.

### What is the difference between a DPS and a dynamic market?

The dynamic market is the Procurement Act 2023’s replacement for the dynamic purchasing system. It must accept new suppliers at any time. DPSs set up under the old rules are still in use.

### Does a place on a framework guarantee work?

No. It lets you compete for, or be awarded, call-off contracts under it. It isn’t a promise of work.

### Can a small firm without audited accounts join a dynamic market?

Yes, if it meets the conditions. Buyers can’t require audited accounts from suppliers that aren’t required to have them audited under the Companies Act 2006, and they must accept alternative evidence of financial capacity.

Title: Social Value in Public Sector Tenders: PPN 002 and PPN 026 | Tendderr
Summary: Social value in public tenders: the 10% minimum weighting under PPN 002, the PPN 026 model from 1 January 2027, and commitments you can deliver.

Guide

# Social value in public tenders: what buyers score and what’s changing

Last checked against official sources: 30 October 2026. General information, not legal advice.

Short answer
Central government buyers must give social value a minimum 10% weighting of the total score in above-threshold procurements under PPN 002. From 1 January 2027, PPN 026 applies to central government procurements of £1 million or more: a minimum 10% weighting from £1m to £5m, and 20% for £5m and over, focused on good jobs and skills. Other public bodies, such as councils, can choose to follow the same approach. Whatever you commit to becomes part of the contract.

## Now: PPN 002

- Applies to central government departments, their executive agencies and non-departmental public bodies, for above-threshold procurements under the Procurement Act 2023.

- A minimum 10% weighting of the total score for social value. Where price-per-quality-point or value-for-money methods are used, it’s 10% of the quality score.

- Commitments made in your tender must go into the contract as terms or key performance indicators.

- Local jobs created to deliver the contract must be advertised through the government’s ‘Find a Job’ website.

- Buyers must avoid placing unnecessary burdens on suppliers, and must have regard to the barriers SMEs and VCSEs face.

- Other public bodies may choose to apply it.

Source: PPN 002 (https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/ppn-002-taking-account-of-social-value-in-the-award-of-contracts/ppn-002-taking-account-of-social-value-in-the-award-of-central-government-contracts-html).

Separately, the Public Services (Social Value) Act 2012 requires public bodies to consider social value when buying services.

## From 1 January 2027: PPN 026 and the new Social Value Model

- Applies to central government covered procurements of £1 million or more (including VAT) that start on or after 1 January 2027.

- Minimum weighting: 10% for contracts from £1m to £5m, and 20% for £5m and over.

- Two outcomes, Good Jobs and Skills, with six award criteria.

- At least one social value key performance indicator on contracts of £5m or more.

- Poor social value performance can be taken into account when considering whether to exclude a supplier.

- Further guidance was due in autumn 2026, and other authorities may adopt the model.

Source: PPN 026: the Social Value Model (https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/ppn-026-the-social-value-model/ppn-026-the-social-value-model-html).

## Writing a social value answer you can deliver

- Answer the question the buyer asked. Use their award criteria and words.

- Commit only to what you can actually deliver. It becomes a contract term or KPI.

- Give each commitment a number, a named owner and a reporting date.

- Keep it proportionate to the size of the contract and your business.

Our social value plan does this for the contract in front of you: £145 as an add-on to a bid pack, or £245 standalone.

## Sources

- PPN 002: taking account of social value in the award of central government contracts (GOV.UK, updated 5 March 2025) (https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/ppn-002-taking-account-of-social-value-in-the-award-of-contracts/ppn-002-taking-account-of-social-value-in-the-award-of-central-government-contracts-html)
- PPN 026: the Social Value Model (GOV.UK, updated 28 October 2026) (https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/ppn-026-the-social-value-model/ppn-026-the-social-value-model-html)

## More guides

- Procurement Act 2023
- CDP registration
- Frameworks, DPS and dynamic markets
- Where to find public-sector tenders

## Quick answers

### How much is social value worth in a public tender?

For central government above-threshold procurements under PPN 002, at least 10% of the total score. Under PPN 026, from 1 January 2027 for central government procurements of £1m or more, at least 10% from £1m to £5m and 20% for £5m and over. Councils and other buyers set their own weightings unless they choose to follow these notes.

### Do councils have to use PPN 002?

PPN 002 applies to central government departments, executive agencies and non-departmental public bodies. Other public bodies may choose to apply it. The Public Services (Social Value) Act 2012 requires public bodies to consider social value for services contracts.

### What happens if we don’t deliver our social value commitments?

Commitments become contract terms or KPIs, so they’re monitored like the rest of the contract. Under PPN 026, poor social value performance can be taken into account when considering exclusion.

### What does PPN 026 change?

From 1 January 2027 it brings in a new Social Value Model for central government procurements of £1m or more. It focuses on Good Jobs and Skills, with minimum weightings of 10% or 20% depending on contract value.

Title: Where to Find Public Sector Tenders (UK and NI) | Tendderr
Summary: Free official portals for public-sector tenders: Find a Tender, Contracts Finder, Sell2Wales, eTendersNI, YORtender and Irish eTenders. Checked October 2026.

Guide

# Where to find public-sector tenders in England, Wales and Northern Ireland

Last checked against official sources: 30 October 2026. General information, not legal advice.

Short answer
Start with Find a Tender, the government’s free central digital platform. Below-threshold notices must now be published there too. Then add the portals your buyers use: Sell2Wales for Wales, eTendersNI for Northern Ireland, regional portals such as YORtender for many Yorkshire councils, and eTenders for the Republic of Ireland. You shouldn’t have to pay to view public-sector opportunities.

## The main portals

Official public-sector tender portals we monitor

| Portal | Covers | Notes | 

| Find a Tender (https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/) | UK-wide | The central digital platform under the Procurement Act 2023. Free for everyone, with free search and alerts. | 

| Contracts Finder (https://www.contractsfinder.service.gov.uk/) | England | Older notices and contracts. Below-threshold notices now go on Find a Tender first. | 

| Sell2Wales (https://www.sell2wales.gov.wales/) | Wales | The Welsh Government’s portal for public-sector opportunities in Wales, including subcontracting opportunities. | 

| eTendersNI (https://www.finance-ni.gov.uk/articles/register-email-alerts-ni-public-sector-tender-opportunities) | Northern Ireland | Free to register. Choose your CPV categories and the account Administrator gets alerts. | 

| YORtender (https://yortender.eu-supply.com/ctm/Company/CompanyRegistration/RegisterCompany?B=UK) | Yorkshire and the Humber | Shared e-tendering portal used by councils such as Wakefield and the West Yorkshire Combined Authority. | 

| eTenders (https://www.etenders.gov.ie/) | Republic of Ireland | The Irish Government’s tenders portal. | 

Sources: Cabinet Office short guide for suppliers (https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/procurement-act-2023-short-guides/the-procurement-act-2023-a-short-guide-for-suppliers-html); GOV.UK below-threshold guidance (https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/procurement-act-2023-guidance-documents-define-phase/guidance-below-threshold-contracts-html); Department of Finance NI (https://www.finance-ni.gov.uk/articles/register-email-alerts-ni-public-sector-tender-opportunities); Wakefield Council (https://www.wakefield.gov.uk/business/procurement-and-tendering/selling-to-the-council); West Yorkshire Combined Authority (https://www.westyorks-ca.gov.uk/governance/procurement/).

## Tenders in Leeds and Yorkshire

Many Yorkshire and Humber public bodies advertise through YORtender, including Wakefield Council and the West Yorkshire Combined Authority. Bigger contracts and below-threshold notices also appear on Find a Tender. It’s worth registering on both and choosing the categories that match your trade. Sources: Wakefield Council (https://www.wakefield.gov.uk/business/procurement-and-tendering/selling-to-the-council); West Yorkshire Combined Authority (https://www.westyorks-ca.gov.uk/governance/procurement/).

## Northern Ireland

eTendersNI is free. Register, choose the CPV categories that match your work, and the Administrator on your account receives email alerts. The Department of Finance lists a helpdesk on 0800 240 4545. Source: Department of Finance NI (https://www.finance-ni.gov.uk/articles/register-email-alerts-ni-public-sector-tender-opportunities).

## Republic of Ireland (Irish eTenders)

Irish public-sector opportunities are advertised on eTenders. If payments to you from a public-sector contract will exceed €10,000 (including VAT) in a year, you need an Irish Tax Clearance Certificate. Construction contracts also need a Relevant Contracts Tax rate of 0% or 20%. Source: Revenue (Ireland) (https://www.revenue.ie/en/starting-a-business/tax-clearance/when-is-a-tax-clearance-certificate-required/to-apply-for-certain-grants-and-public-sector-contracts.aspx).

## Let us do the searching

Our free tender alert covers all of these. A person checks each match against your trade and area, and our contract renewal alerts flag contracts nearing expiry. Not ready to bid direct? The subcontracting route pack (£195) finds the main contractors winning work near you.

## Quick answers

### Where are UK public-sector tenders published?

On Find a Tender, the government’s free central digital platform. Below-threshold notices must be published there too. Many buyers also use regional or sector portals, such as Sell2Wales, eTendersNI and YORtender.

### Are tender portals free?

Find a Tender is free, and the government says you shouldn’t pay to view public-sector opportunities. eTendersNI is also free to register.

### Where do Yorkshire councils advertise tenders?

Many use YORtender, the shared Yorkshire and Humber e-tendering portal, as well as Find a Tender.

### Do I need tax clearance to bid for Irish public contracts?

You need an Irish Tax Clearance Certificate if payments from a public-sector contract will exceed €10,000 including VAT in a year, according to Revenue.

# Privacy notice

Last updated: 31 October 2026

Don't want to hear from us? Reply to any of our emails, or email hello@tendderr.com with the word ‘unsubscribe’. We'll add you to our suppression list and won't contact you again.

This notice explains what personal information Tendderr holds, why, and what your rights are. We've tried to keep it short and in plain English.

## Who we are

Tendderr is a trading name of Mark Hutchinson, a sole trader, of Ground Floor, Radley House, Richardshaw Road, Leeds, LS28 6LE, United Kingdom. We are the controller of the personal information described in this notice.

For any privacy question or request, email us at hello@tendderr.com, call 0333 339 7931 or write to us at the address above.

## What information we hold

- Business contact details: names, job titles, business email addresses, business phone numbers and business addresses of people at contracting firms we think may benefit from our service.

- Correspondence: emails and other messages you send us, and our replies, including details you give us about your business and the work you're interested in.

- Work information: if you use our tender alert, suitability check or bid preparation, the information needed to provide that service.

We don't seek or hold sensitive (special category) information.

## Where we get it

We collect business contact details from public sources, such as Companies House and company websites. Otherwise, we get information directly from you when you contact us or use our service.

## How we use it

- To contact businesses about our tender alert, suitability check and bid preparation services.

- To reply to your enquiries and provide the services you ask for.

- To keep a suppression list so we respect opt-outs.

- To keep the business records we're required to keep by law.

## Our legal basis

Under the UK GDPR, we rely on legitimate interests (Article 6(1)(f)) to contact people at businesses about services that are relevant to their work. Our interest is in telling contractors about a service that may help them win public-sector work. We keep this contact proportionate: we only use business contact details, we only contact businesses whose work relates to what we offer, and you can opt out at any time.

Where you ask us to provide a service, we process your information to take steps at your request and to perform our agreement with you (Article 6(1)(b)). Where the law requires us to keep records, we rely on legal obligation (Article 6(1)(c)).

## Electronic marketing rules (PECR)

The Privacy and Electronic Communications Regulations (PECR) allow businesses to send marketing emails to corporate subscribers (such as limited companies, limited liability partnerships, Scottish partnerships and public bodies) without prior consent, provided the sender is identified and a simple way to opt out is given in every message. We only send unsolicited emails to corporate addresses on that basis, and every email we send tells you who we are and how to opt out.

We will not send unsolicited marketing emails to sole traders or to partnerships in England, Wales and Northern Ireland, who count as individual subscribers under PECR, unless they have agreed to hear from us.

## How to opt out

You can object to our contact at any time, for free. Reply to any of our emails, or email hello@tendderr.com with ‘unsubscribe’. We'll stop contacting you and add your email address to our suppression list. We keep that minimal record only so that we don't contact you again.

## Who we share it with

We do not sell, rent or trade your information. We only share it with service providers who help us run the business, such as our email and file storage providers, and only so they can provide those services to us. We may also disclose information if the law requires it.

## How long we keep it

- Business contact details for people who haven't engaged with us: up to 12 months from our last contact, then deleted.

- Correspondence and client records: as long as needed to provide the service, and then for as long as the law requires us to keep business records.

- Suppression list entries: kept for as long as we market our services, so that we respect your opt-out.

## Your rights

You have the right to:

- ask for a copy of the personal information we hold about you

- ask us to correct anything that's inaccurate

- ask us to delete your information

- ask us to restrict how we use it

- object to our use of it, including an absolute right to object to direct marketing

To use any of these rights, email hello@tendderr.com. We'll respond within one month.

## Complaints

If you're unhappy with how we've handled your information, please tell us first and we'll try to put it right. You also have the right to complain to the Information Commissioner's Office (ICO), the UK's data protection regulator, at ico.org.uk (https://ico.org.uk) or on 0303 123 1113.

## This website

This website does not use cookies, analytics or tracking of any kind, and has no forms that send information to us. Our free tools (the readiness checker, timeline calculator and social value checklist) run entirely in your browser: nothing you enter in them is sent to us or stored. If you email us, we handle your message as described above.

### Chat assistant

Our website has an optional ‘Ask us’ assistant that answers questions about our service by text or voice. It is an automated assistant, not a person, and it can make mistakes, so please check anything important with us by email.

The assistant is provided by ElevenLabs, which processes your messages for us. If you use it, we receive a written record (transcript) of the conversation. We don't keep voice recordings. We keep transcripts for up to 12 months and then delete them. We use them only to answer your questions and to improve the assistant.

Please don't share sensitive personal information in the chat. If you'd like us to follow up, email hello@tendderr.com instead. To show the chat button, your browser loads the assistant from ElevenLabs and the unpkg content network when you visit a page, which means they will see your IP address.

## Changes to this notice

We may update this notice from time to time. The date at the top shows when it last changed.
